items.text: CBS News live (June 13): Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who has been the lead mediator throughout the negotiations, posted on Friday that 'a final, agreed upon text' of the US-Iran peace deal had been reached and Pakistan was 'now working closely with both sides to finalize the next steps.' On Saturday, Sharif escalated the timeline: 'We are closer to a peace deal than ever before. With finalisation likely expected in the next 24 hours, Pakistan is preparing for the electronic signing of the peace deal immediately after, followed by technical level talks next week.' Sharif tagged President Trump, Vice President Vance, Iranian President Pezeshkian, and regional leaders in the post — signalling maximum diplomatic visibility. This is the clearest Pakistan mediator statement of the entire 106-day process, going beyond 'we are close' to specifying a mechanism (electronic signing) and a timeline (24 hours) and a next step (technical talks).

items.text: CNBC, Bloomberg, CBS News (June 13): Trump posted on Truth Social on Saturday: 'The Deal is scheduled to get signed tomorrow, and immediately after it is signed, the Hormuz Strait is OPEN TO ALL.' Hours later, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei told IRIB: 'Although it will not happen tomorrow, the possibility that it could take place in the coming days cannot be ruled out. However, given the other side's inconsistency, we must remain cautious in making any statements about the process.' Iran also clarified that the Islamabad MOU 'is focused on ending the war, and at this stage it has been decided that the nuclear issue will not be addressed' — a significant public statement that contradicts CBS News sources reporting the MOU commits Iran to a 15-20 year nuclear lockout with dismantlement of nuclear sites. This nuclear ambiguity — Iran publicly says no nuclear terms, but sources say 15-20yr lockout is in the MOU — is the most significant unresolved gap heading into Sunday. Polymarket: US-Iran peace deal final text agreed on June 12; Trump signals imminent signing, but Iranian officials describe reports as 'preliminary' with nuclear issues requiring 'separate follow-on negotiations.'

items.text: CBS News live, CNN (June 12-13): Even as the deal framework was being finalised, the US military intercepted multiple Iranian attack drones targeting commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz — once on Friday night and again on Saturday. Trump posted on Saturday that the drone attacks were 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE,' while separately announcing the deal would be signed Sunday. The disconnect — Trump claiming imminent deal while condemning simultaneous Iranian military action — captures the extraordinary ambiguity of the final stretch of negotiations. Separately, a CNN/Israeli source confirmed Israel is pressing the US to prevent the unfreezing of Iranian assets as part of the ceasefire agreement. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said Israel will not withdraw from the territories it occupies in Lebanon. PM Netanyahu said: 'As long as I am the Prime Minister of Israel, Iran will not have nuclear weapons.' Iran's FM Araghchi had said Friday that both sides were working toward an agreement ending the war 'on all fronts, including Lebanon' — making the Lebanon question (and Israel's refusal to withdraw) a potential deal-breaker even at the last moment.

items.text: CBS News live (June 13): US Secretary of State Marco Rubio discussed the Settebello strike — in which three Indian sailors were killed by US Navy precision munitions on June 9-10 — with India's External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar. The US State Department readout was notably unapologetic: 'The Secretary stressed that all commercial vessels should immediately comply with orders from U.S. forces as they seek to uphold peace and security in the Strait. He underscored that violations of the U.S. blockade and the illicit transport of Iranian oil will not be tolerated.' India's MEA responded in a separate statement that 'the Ministry once again conveyed its deep concern over the use of lethal and deadly force against civilian shipping. Such actions are unacceptable and undermine the safety, security and stability of international maritime commerce in a sensitive region at a difficult time.' The divergence in tone — the US defending the strike, India condemning it — sets up the Modi-Trump bilateral at G7 Evian-les-Bains (June 15-17) as a high-stakes diplomatic encounter on this specific issue.

items.bold: KHAMENEI FUNERAL announced for July 4 (multi-day, Tehran/Qom/Mashhad), burial July 9 at Imam Reza Shrine. First formal state funeral announcement since his death on Day 1 (Feb 28). MOU nuclear ambiguity: Iran says no nuclear terms; CBS sources say 15-20yr lockout in deal.
items.text: CBS News live (June 13): Iran announced that the funeral for former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei — killed in the joint US-Israeli strike on Day 1 of the war, February 28 — will begin July 4, with a multi-day procession through Tehran, Qom, and Mashhad before his burial at the Imam Reza Shrine in Mashhad on July 9. This is the first formal announcement of state funeral arrangements in the 106 days since his death. The timing — July 4, US Independence Day — may be deliberate or coincidental. The nuclear ambiguity in the deal is the most significant unresolved policy question: Iran's FM Baghaei publicly stated the MOU does not address nuclear issues; but multiple CBS News sources say the MOU commits Iran to not enrich uranium for 15-20 years and to dismantle its nuclear sites — conditions that, if true, represent the most significant arms control achievement since the 2015 JCPOA. The divergence between Iran's public position ('no nuclear terms') and what Western sources say the document contains ('15-20yr lockout') will become clear only when (if) the text is made public.

military.t: DEAL IMMINENT — Trump: Signed Sunday Jun 14 + 'Hormuz OPEN TO ALL immediately after.' Pakistan: 'Electronic Signing Ready.' Iran: NOT Sunday, 'Coming Days.' Final text agreed Jun 12. Nuclear ambiguity unresolved.
military.d: CNBC, Bloomberg, CBS News, NPR (June 12-13): Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif confirmed on Friday June 12 that 'a final, agreed upon text of the US-Iran peace deal has been reached.' Trump posted on Truth Social Saturday: 'The Deal is scheduled to get signed tomorrow (June 14), and immediately after it is signed, the Hormuz Strait is OPEN TO ALL.' Pakistan PM on Saturday: finalisation 'likely in next 24 hours' — Pakistan is 'preparing for the electronic signing immediately after, followed by technical level talks next week.' Iran FM spokesperson Baghaei, however, said Saturday evening the deal would not be signed Sunday: 'Although it will not happen tomorrow, the possibility that it could take place in the coming days cannot be ruled out. Given the other side's inconsistency, we must remain cautious.' The nuclear ambiguity is the core unresolved issue: Iran publicly says the MOU does not address nuclear issues; CBS News sources say the text commits Iran to a 15-20 year enrichment lockout and dismantlement of nuclear sites — a gap that will define the deal's reception in Iran domestically, and determine whether Israel ultimately accepts it.

military.t: US SHOT DOWN Iranian Attack Drones in Hormuz — FRIDAY NIGHT + SATURDAY. Trump: 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE.' Drones Fired Even as Deal Text Was Being Finalised. Ceasefire Violations Continue Until Ink Dries.
military.d: CBS News live (June 12-13): The US military shot down multiple Iranian attack drones targeting commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday night, and again on Saturday. Trump condemned the attacks on Saturday as 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE' — in the same social media window where he was announcing the deal would be signed Sunday. The juxtaposition captures how fragile the 'deal imminent' narrative is: even as the text is being finalised and signatures are being coordinated, Iran continues to target Hormuz-transit vessels with armed drones. This pattern — military activity + diplomatic activity simultaneously — has been the defining characteristic of the entire conflict. Until ink is dry on the MOU and Hormuz begins active de-mining, the Strait remains effectively closed and actively contested. CNN reported that under the agreement, the waterway would not return to exactly how it operated before the war — suggesting a new governance model (likely involving the Iran-Oman PGSA framework, modified) will apply post-deal.

assessment.body:
Sunday 7:15 AM IST. Day 106. Two days of catch-up (Days 104-106).

WHAT HAPPENED SINCE FRIDAY

FRIDAY (Day 104):
The biggest market rally of the 106-day war.
Nifty +461 pts (+1.99%) to 23,623. Sensex +1,695 pts (+2.3%) to 75,528.
VIX crashed -5.7% to 14.72 — lowest since the war began.
Brent fell ~4% to ~$87. WTI closed under $85.
Pakistan PM: 'final agreed-upon text has been reached.'
Iran FM Araghchi: both sides working toward deal 'on all fronts, including Lebanon.'
US shot down Iranian attack drones in Hormuz Friday night (still happening even as deal finalises).

SATURDAY (Day 105):
Trump Truth Social: 'The Deal is scheduled to get signed TOMORROW (June 14),
and immediately after it is signed, the Hormuz Strait is OPEN TO ALL.'
Pakistan PM: finalisation 'likely in next 24 hours,' preparing for
'electronic signing immediately after + technical level talks next week.'
But Iran FM Baghaei Saturday evening: NOT Sunday.
'Coming days possible. Given the other side's inconsistency, remain cautious.'
Iran publicly states nuclear issue WILL NOT be addressed in the MOU.
CBS sources: the MOU commits Iran to a 15-20 year enrichment lockout + dismantlement.
US shot down more Iranian drones in Hormuz. Trump: 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE.'
Israel pressed US against unfreezing Iranian assets. Katz: not leaving Lebanon.
Netanyahu: 'as long as I am PM, Iran will not have nuclear weapons.'
Khamenei funeral announced: July 4 (Tehran, Qom, Mashhad), burial July 9 Mashhad.
Rubio-Jaishankar call: US defended Settebello; India MEA: 'lethal force unacceptable.'

THE MOMENT OF TRUTH — TODAY, JUNE 14
Trump says signed today. Iran says not today.
Pakistan is ready with electronic signing infrastructure.
The nuclear terms gap is real — if public, risks Iran's domestic ratification.
Israel's blocking on asset unfreezing + Lebanon is the other structural obstacle.
G7 starts tomorrow (June 15) in Evian-les-Bains — a hard deadline for both sides.

IF THE DEAL IS SIGNED TODAY:
Brent crashes to $78-82 (pre-war: $65, war peak: $111).
Nifty surges to 24,500-25,000 in coming sessions.
Sensex tests 78,000-80,000.
Rupee strengthens to Rs91-93/USD.
LPG/petrol/diesel prices — government to cut by Rs2-4/L in coming weeks.
18,000+ Indian seafarers in Gulf begin repatriation.
Indian seafarer deaths (3, MT Settebello) go to G7 bilateral as diplomatic repair.
OMC stocks (BPCL, IOC, HPCL): massive gap-up on Monday.

IF THE DEAL IS NOT SIGNED TODAY:
Brent likely bounces back toward $89-93.
Nifty may give back some Friday gains.
Markets reprice the 40th false dawn.
Trump's credibility in Iran-deal claims at a new low.
Risk of renewed Kharg Island threat if Iran delays beyond this week.

India has the most at stake of any third party.
Three sailors dead. 18,000 seafarers at risk.
Energy at Rs111/L petrol, Rs941/cylinder LPG.
The deal, if it comes today, ends all three crises simultaneously.
